execution_contract.invocation: subprocess.run([sys.executable, 'scripts/main.py', ...], cwd=<runtime>, shell=False, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=...)
execution_contract.cwd: the runtime copy root (required: model/best_model.pth, model/mismatch_model.pth, ./toxicity/cell_viability.txt, ./off-target/*, ./data/infer/*, scripts/RNA-FM.sh are all relative paths)
execution_contract.offtarget_env_resolution: env OLIGOFORMER_OFFTARGET_ENV, else parents[2]/'deps'/'offtarget-env' (perl + RNAplfald checked in <env>/bin)
execution_contract.runtime_identity_check: scripts/main.py, scripts/infer.py, scripts/mismatch.py, scripts/RNA-FM.sh, model/best_model.pth, model/mismatch_model.pth, toxicity/cell_viability.txt and RNA-FM/torch_home/hub/checkpoints/RNA-FM_pretrained.pth must exist, and scripts/main.py must contain 'OligoFormer' and '--infer'; otherwise ToolError (an executable bit / exit 0 alone is not accepted)

child_env.PATH: os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(sys.executable)) [+ <offtarget-env>/bin for -off] + inherited PATH; NOT Path(sys.executable).resolve(), because the venv's bin/python is a symlink to the base interpreter whose bin directory has no torch (observed failure: RNA-FM.sh's bare 'python' raised ModuleNotFoundError: torch and the run died in loader.py)
child_env.TORCH_HOME: <runtime>/RNA-FM/torch_home (RNA-FM loads its checkpoint from the torch.hub cache; no download)
child_env.PERL5LIB: removed, so the conda perl finds its own BioPerl/Statistics::Lite

execution_contract.diagnostics: stdout/stderr captured, never printed; written to <run_dir>/logs/<label>.{stdout,stderr}.log plus the exact command; a nonzero exit or a timeout raises fastmcp.exceptions.ToolError with a 4000-char tail of each stream

tools.name: predict_sirna_efficacy_from_mrna
tools.upstream_implementation: scripts/infer.py:infer, Args.infer == 1 with falsy Args.infer_siRNA_fasta (antiRNA window traversal, calculate_td, func_filter, scripts/RNA-FM.sh, loader.py:data_process_loader_infer, model.py:Oligo + model/best_model.pth)

parameters.mrna_fasta_path: required; no default (never loads the bundled data/example.fa)
parameters.apply_functionality_filter: bool = True; False maps to upstream -nf. Default True keeps upstream's default behaviour (the func_filter column present).
parameters.include_toxicity: bool = False; True maps to -tox. Default False is upstream's default (no toxicity columns).
parameters.toxicity_threshold: float = 50.0, upstream's --toxicity_threshold default; only meaningful together with include_toxicity and passed only then
parameters.output_dir: optional base; a fresh subdirectory predict_mrna_<utc>_<uuid8> is created per call. Default base: <project>/tmp/outputs/cli_wrapper.

tools.excluded_upstream_options: -off/-a/-top (own tool / defects, see excluded_options), --infer 2, training and test flags, model hyper-parameters (--vocab_size, --lstm_dim, ... belong to training), --seed (see stochasticity), --best_model, --path
tools.outputs: <run_dir>/<record>.txt, <record>_ranked.txt, <record>_ranked_filtered.txt (upstream's own tables, written directly by the CLI into the fresh directory) plus <run_dir>/windows/<record>/{siRNA.fa,mRNA.fa} copied out of the scratch directory; returned fields: records, windows_per_record, per_record_summary (rows, columns, func_filter_counts, rows_passing_filter, ranked_filtered_rows, missing-value counts), output_dir, stochastic_efficacy

tools.name: predict_specific_sirna_efficacy
tools.upstream_implementation: scripts/infer.py:infer, Args.infer == 1 with the `if Args.infer_siRNA_fasta:` branch (re.search(antiRNA(siRNA), mRNA) site location, +-19 nt flanked context)
tools.parameters: mrna_fasta_path, sirna_fasta_path (both required), then the same filter parameters and output_dir as predict_sirna_efficacy_from_mrna
tools.outputs: the same three tables per scored record; returned fields: records_scored, matched_sirnas_per_record, unmatched_records, unmatched_sirnas, per_record_summary, output_dir, stochastic_efficacy. The message states that 'pos' is a row counter over matched siRNAs (not a transcript position) and that only the first site per record is scored.

tools.name: screen_sirna_offtarget
tools.upstream_implementation: scripts/infer.py:infer `if Args.off_target:` with Args.top_n == -1, which os.system's scripts/pita.sh (off-target/pita/pita_prediction.pl, RNAplfold, perl Statistics::Lite/Bio::TreeIO) and scripts/targetscan.sh (off-target/targetscan/targetscan_70*.pl), then merges data/infer/<record>/{pita.tab,targetscan.tab}

parameters.utr_reference_path: optional; default <runtime>/off-target/ref/100_human_UTR.txt (upstream default). User paths must exist, be non-empty and contain no space/shell metacharacter, because infer.py interpolates them unquoted into os.system('bash scripts/pita.sh ...').
parameters.other: apply_functionality_filter / include_toxicity / toxicity_threshold / output_dir as in tool 1

tools.outputs: the three result tables per record (now with pita_score, targetscan_score, off_target_filter) plus <run_dir>/offtarget/<record>/{pita.tab,targetscan.tab,siRNA.fa}; returned fields add pita_rows per record and the resolved utr/orf reference paths
tools.timeout: 3600 s + 60 s per 19-nt window (reference runs took ~7 min for the 78 windows of data/example.fa)

tools.name: compare_sirna_mismatch_kon
tools.upstream_implementation: scripts/mismatch.py:mismatch, Args.mismatch == 1 branch -> calculate_kon with the module-level MismatchModule from model/mismatch_model.pth (model.eval() is called; deterministic)
tools.parameters: base_rna, mismatched_rna (required; each validated as exactly 19 nt of A/C/G/U)
tools.outputs: no files (artifacts: []); returns kon (float), base_rna, mismatched_rna, num_mismatches, mismatch_positions
tools.stdout_parsing: input() prompts are printed to stdout even with piped stdin; the tool requires exit 0 and parses the last non-empty stdout line with float()

tools.name: scan_sirna_mismatch_variants
tools.upstream_implementation: scripts/mismatch.py:mismatch else-branch -> generate_mismatch_sequences + calculate_kon, writing Args.output_dir + '/result/mismatch.txt'

parameters.base_rna: required; validated as exactly 19 nt of A/C/G/U
parameters.max_mismatches: Literal[2, 3] = 2, mapped to upstream -m 2 / -m 3. 2 -> 1596 rows (~6 s); 3 -> 27759 rows (~95 s).
parameters.output_dir: optional base; fresh mismatch_scan_<utc>_<uuid8> subdirectory per call

tools.outputs: <run_dir>/result/mismatch.txt (seq, kon, num_mismatch); returns num_rows, columns, rows_per_num_mismatch

io_adaptations.adaptation: Fresh per-call output directory with a UTC timestamp plus 8 hex characters of uuid4, created inside the function (not at import).
io_adaptations.justification: A persistent MCP server must distinguish repeated requests; upstream string-concatenates --output_dir, so the directory is passed with a trailing separator for --infer (infer.py: Args.output_dir + name + '.txt') and WITHOUT one for -m, where mismatch.py concatenates '/result/mismatch.txt' and needs <dir>/result to exist (pre-created by the wrapper).

io_adaptations.adaptation: Global serialization of every tool execution: a threading.Lock plus an fcntl.flock on <runtime>/.cli_wrapper.lock.
io_adaptations.justification: Upstream writes fixed in-tree paths: ./data/infer/<record>/ (rm -rf + mkdir per record), ./result/, off-target/pita/* and off-target/tmp (created and removed by targetscan.sh). Executor evidence (infer_offtarget_toxicity, infer_offtarget_top_n hazards) shows concurrent runs in one tree clobber each other.

io_adaptations.adaptation: After each run, per-record intermediates are copied out of ./data/infer/<record> (siRNA.fa/mRNA.fa, and pita.tab/targetscan.tab for off-target) and the per-record scratch directories are removed with shutil.rmtree.
io_adaptations.justification: loader.py reads from that fixed location, so it cannot be redirected; the executors copied the same files per run. Removing the scratch avoids stale state after a crash (hazard recorded in infer_offtarget_top_n). The empty ./data/infer parent and the files upstream itself writes under off-target/pita are left in place: removing tracked runtime files is not the wrapper's business.

io_adaptations.adaptation: mRNA FASTA validation: header must match ^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$ and be unique; each record >= 19 nt; sequence characters restricted to A/C/G/T/U.
io_adaptations.justification: Record names are interpolated unquoted into os.system('rm -rf ./data/infer/' + name) and the pita/targetscan commands (injection and corruption risk), and spaces are mangled to '_@_' in output filenames. '>= 19 nt' is upstream's own requirement (Exception 'The length of mRNA is less than 19 nt!'). infer.py:antiRNA silently drops characters outside A/U/C/G/T/X, which would shift the window sequences, so other letters (N, IUPAC codes) are rejected with a clear message instead of producing misleading rows. Documented limitation: headers with spaces are not supported.

io_adaptations.adaptation: siRNA FASTA validation: every non-header line must match ^[ACGU]{19}$; blank lines are reported as invalid; no case folding and no T->U conversion.
io_adaptations.justification: infer.py raises 'The length of some siRNA is not 19 nt!' for any other length (executor case error_len20, exit 1) and, unlike the mRNA path, does not upper-case or convert T for siRNA input, so lowercase/DNA input would reach the model unchanged. Silently converting would alter the user's scientific input, so it is rejected with an explanatory error.

io_adaptations.adaptation: predict_specific_sirna_efficacy pre-scans which records contain a match (re.search(_anti_rna(siRNA), mRNA.upper().replace('T','U')), the same rule as infer.py) and passes upstream a FASTA containing only records with >= 1 match, in one run; unmatched records and unmatched siRNAs are returned.
io_adaptations.justification: Executor infer_specific_sirnas error_zero_match_RNA1: a record with zero matching siRNAs makes RNA-FM.sh fail silently and loader.py raise FileNotFoundError('./data/infer/RNA1/siRNA.fa'), exit 1, which aborts the whole run so later records get no output at all. The pre-scan changes only which records are handed to the CLI, not how matching or scoring is done (that stays in infer.py). _anti_rna is a 4-letter reverse-complement helper used solely for routing, mirroring infer.py:antiRNA for the validated A/C/G/U alphabet; it is not used in any scored computation. If no siRNA matches any record, the tool raises a clear ToolError instead of running.

io_adaptations.adaptation: Off-target result verification after a zero exit: data/infer/<record>/pita.tab must have the header RefSeq/microRNA/Sites/Score and at least one data row, targetscan.tab must be non-empty, and pita_score / targetscan_score must not be missing for every row of the result table.
io_adaptations.justification: infer.py calls pita.sh and targetscan.sh through os.system and ignores their status. Executor infer_offtarget_toxicity reproduced the silent-failure mode with the README '-a' variant: exit 0, header-only pita.tab, 0-byte targetscan.tab, all scores NaN and off_target_filter 0 for every row, i.e. every siRNA falsely passing. Reference-file existence and non-emptiness are checked for the same reason.

io_adaptations.adaptation: Result-table presence check for every tool: <record>.txt must exist and have >= 1 data row, else ToolError.
io_adaptations.justification: The RNA-FM embedding step also runs through os.system with an unchecked status, so a zero exit from main.py does not establish that the tables were produced.

io_adaptations.adaptation: Bounded timeouts, scaled per window (infer 900 s + 30 s/window; off-target 3600 s + 60 s/window; mismatch pair 600 s; mismatch scan 3600 s), and stdin always supplied (empty string when unused).
io_adaptations.justification: Runtime scales linearly with mRNA length (one RNA-FM forward pass per window); --infer 2 and the mismatch modes read stdin with input(), so a child must never be left waiting for a terminal.

stochasticity.finding: scripts/infer.py never calls model.eval() and never seeds torch, while scripts/model.py keeps nn.Dropout(0.02) layers active, so the efficacy column varies run to run: executors measured up to 0.183 absolute / 31.5% relative differences and always-different ranked order, with all other columns byte-identical.
stochasticity.wrapper_behaviour: Not repaired (no eval(), no seeding, no rescaling of the sigmoid * 1.341 output). Every efficacy-producing tool returns stochastic_efficacy: true and states the effect in its message and tool description. No seed parameter is exposed, because main.py --seed only seeds random/numpy/PYTHONHASHSEED and not torch.
stochasticity.mismatch_tools: scripts/mismatch.py calls model.eval() on a CNN without dropout; the executors measured byte-identical repeats, so those tools are reported as deterministic.

excluded_options.reason: Upstream defect confirmed by executor infer_offtarget_top_n: the top-N FASTA writes headers from RESULT_ranked.index[i] (positional) but sequences from RESULT_ranked['siRNA'][i] (label-based), so 8-10 of 10 entries per file carry a sequence from the wrong row and the PITA/TargetScan scores are merged onto rows that were never scored. There is also no bounds check (-top 50 on 39 windows -> IndexError, exit 1). Exposing it would return mislabelled off-target scores; fixing it in the wrapper would mean replacing upstream's selection logic, which is out of scope.

infer.py sets BOTH Args.utr and Args.orf to './off-target/ref/human_UTR.txt', which ships only as human_UTR.txt.zip; executor infer_offtarget_toxicity ran it and got exit 0 with cp/cat/awk 'No such file' errors, header-only pita.tab, 0-byte targetscan.tab and all-NaN scores, i.e. a silent false pass for every siRNA.

Interactive duplicate of the --infer 1 traversal with the record name hard-coded to RNA0 (so concurrent calls collide in data/infer/RNA0 and result/RNA0*.txt) and a single sequence only; a one-record FASTA through predict_sirna_efficacy_from_mrna covers the same task.

Deferred by the scanner with a blocker: loader.py requires data/RNAFM/<dataset>_{siRNA,mRNA}/representations/*.npy, which are absent from the pinned repository and are not regenerated by the test paths; metrics are only written into a log file.

README requires an NVIDIA GPU (~60 min on a V100) and train.py first rebuilds the missing RNA-FM embeddings; it also consumes only the bundled datasets, so it is not an operation on user input. No reference execution exists.
Does not seed torch, so exposing it would promise reproducibility the runtime does not provide.
